taskTitle: Where ten HTTP header fields are defined

checks.detail: 4 subtasks, read from the schema reply
6 phases had the tools designed for them

finalText:
I have not opened any pages myself. This answer rests entirely on the four worker reports, and the quotes are as the workers copied them. I could not re-check them against the pages.

**Findings**
- **Age, Cache-Control, Expires** are defined in RFC 9111, in sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3 respectively (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html). The page says it obsoletes RFC 7234, and it shows no later replacement. That worker also searched for "RFC 9111 obsoleted by" and found nothing.
- **Last-Modified, ETag, Vary** are defined in RFC 9110, in sections 8.8.2, 8.8.3 and 12.5.5 respectively (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html). RFC 9110 obsoletes RFC 7231 and RFC 7232. Its header shows no "Obsoleted by" line, but that worker checked no other source.
- **Location, Retry-After** are defined in RFC 9110, in sections 10.2.2 and 10.2.3 respectively (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html). That worker also found no sign that RFC 9110 has been obsoleted, and did not check the RFC Editor's metadata for it.
- **Strict-Transport-Security** is defined in RFC 6797, section 6.1 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6797.html).
- **Link** is defined in RFC 8288, section 3 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8288.html). RFC 8288 obsoletes RFC 5988.

**Caveat on "currently defines"**
Every "not obsoleted" conclusion rests on the opened RFC pages showing no "Obsoleted by" text, plus one search for RFC 9111. For RFC 6797 and RFC 8288 the RFC Editor info pages returned 404, so neither could be checked against the RFC index. No worker reported conflicting sources.
